Order decides it, not band. THE INSTRUMENT LESSON: because all legs share one account, XP is NOT comparable across legs of the same lesson, and no finding may be built on that comparison. I built one on a verifier's aside without checking the mechanism; a re-cite agent checked it and refuted it.

what: BOTH TOUCH SLIDERS ANNOUNCE A RANGE AND ALWAYS REPORT ZERO. platform/src/components/sim/TouchControls.tsx declares role="slider" with aria-valuemin={-100} and aria-valuemax={100} on the steering wheel (line 2354, «Волан — плъзни наляво или надясно») and on the drive axis (line ~2403, driveAxisLabelBg), and hardcodes aria-valuenow={0} as a LITERAL on both — lines 2357 and 2408. Neither is ever updated; the knob is moved through a ref, so the visible control tracks the gesture while the accessibility value stays at centre. A screen-reader user therefore gets no steering feedback and no throttle/brake feedback at full lock or full pedal: the control reports itself as centred at every position it can reach. Declaring valuemin/valuemax and then pinning valuenow is worse than omitting the role, because it advertises a readable range that does not exist. The audience is 17-18-year-olds on phones and the touch pad is the ONLY control surface on mobile. Surfaced when a controller closed around the slider value would have measured its own commands as having no effect forever — the same defect a blind student meets.
